searchText: <SamWilsn> > <SamWilsn> Might bear repeating on https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-2294-explicit-bound-to-chain-id/11090 (re @eth1x_bridge_bot: <meridian (Sam Bacha)> [reply]: The value used for metamask is MAX_SAFE_CHAIN_ID = floor( ( 2**53 - 39 ) / 2 ) = 4503599627370476 The EIP states: 9,223,372,036,854,775,771 (MAX_CHAIN_ID). This value is floor(MAX_UINT64 / 2) - 36,, which will have issues I added details here https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/issues/2294#issuecomment-1297145918) At Arbitrum we initially tried to use a hash function to produce the L2 chain id (it'd make a lot of sense for it to be the hash of the L1 chain id and rollup contract address for instance) but we ran into a lot of tooling problems. I don't remember the details but I think Ledger (the hardware wallet) had a small chain id limit that made it not work with some early testnets. This might be it https://github.com/LedgerHQ/app-ethereum/issues/283 There is a possibility to turn off Ethash verification post-Merge. What is the scenario where you would want to keep it? The opposite. I want to know how much I have to keep. What is the alternative? I get a hash from CL and download backwards? What about uncles? Yes, this is the only way to sync post-merge and you don't have to verify Ethash anymore. There are no uncles post-Merge and there is no uncle processing, the must always be empty Hi guys, wondering if we have a final decision on how to calculate ForkId. are we just including Timestamps in the CRC calculation. and What about the next value. shall it be the timestamp for the next fork? From my pov thats that would be the easiest solution Will there be a spec, or should we just go with that for now for the next devnet? There will be a spec eventually, we can just decide to do it now and write the spec later

excerpts.content:
<SamWilsn> > <SamWilsn>  Might bear repeating on https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-2294-explicit-bound-to-chain-id/11090 (re @eth1x_bridge_bot: <meridian (Sam Bacha)> [reply]: The value used for metamask is 

MAX_SAFE_CHAIN_ID = floor( ( 2**53 - 39 ) / 2 ) = 4503599627370476

The EIP states: 9,223,372,036,854,775,771 (MAX_CHAIN_ID). This value is floor(MAX_UINT64 / 2) - 36,, which will have issues 


I added details here https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/issues/2294#issuecomment-1297145918)

excerpts.author: plasmapower
excerpts.content: At Arbitrum we initially tried to use a hash function to produce the L2 chain id (it'd make a lot of sense for it to be the hash of the L1 chain id and rollup contract address for instance) but we ran into a lot of tooling problems. I don't remember the details but I think Ledger (the hardware wallet) had a small chain id limit that made it not work with some early testnets.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: There is a possibility to turn off Ethash verification post-Merge. What is the scenario where you would want to keep it?

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content: The opposite. I want to know how much I have to keep.

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content: What is the alternative? I get a hash from CL and download backwards?

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: Yes, this is the only way to sync post-merge and you don't have to verify Ethash anymore. There are no uncles post-Merge and there is no uncle processing, the must always be empty
